intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day speedboat tour around the stunning Phi Phi Islands, including Maya Bay, Monkey Beach, and Pileh Lagoon. Snorkel in crystal-clear turquoise waters teeming with colorful marine life, explore hidden sea caves, and soak in dramatic limestone karst scenery. Lunch and snorkeling gear are typically included.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Beachfront Street Food Night Market
experiences.description: Stroll along the vibrant beachfront night market on Koh Lanta, sampling authentic Thai street food including pad thai, mango sticky rice, fresh grilled seafood, satay skewers, and tropical fruit shakes. Enjoy the laid-back island atmosphere with local vendors and ocean breezes as the backdrop for an unforgettable culinary evening.
experiences.location: Klong Dao Beach, Koh Lanta, Krabi Province

experiences.name: Similan Islands Liveaboard Diving & Snorkeling Experience
experiences.description: Join a two-day liveaboard trip to the world-renowned Similan Islands, one of Thailand's top dive destinations. Explore pristine coral reefs, swim alongside whale sharks and manta rays, and relax on powdery white-sand beaches. The trip includes meals, snorkeling equipment, and guided dives for certified divers or beginner snorkelers.

experiences.name: Chaweng Beach Muay Thai & Cultural Evening Show
experiences.description: Watch an electrifying live Muay Thai boxing match at a beachside stadium on Koh Samui, followed by a traditional Thai cultural performance featuring classical dance and music. This immersive evening gives you a front-row seat to Thailand's national sport and rich artistic heritage, all within walking distance of the beach.
experiences.location: Chaweng Beach, Koh Samui, Surat Thani Province

experiences.name: Railay Beach Rock Climbing & Sunset Kayaking
experiences.description: Spend a thrilling day at the iconic Railay Beach, accessible only by longtail boat. In the morning, take a guided beginner rock climbing session up the dramatic limestone cliffs with panoramic sea views. In the afternoon, rent a sea kayak and paddle through mangroves, hidden lagoons, and sea caves before watching a breathtaking sunset over the Andaman Sea.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport, clear customs, and take a shared minivan or budget bus to the nearest pier (Rassada Pier in Phuket or Ao Nang in Krabi). Board a ferry to Phi Phi Islands. Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a slow walk around Tonsai Village to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Tonsai Bay beachfront, watch the sunset from the pier area, and explore the lively night market stalls near the village center.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at the airport before or after landing — look for 7-Eleven or airport food courts for budget bites (150–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Eat on the ferry or grab a quick pad thai or fried rice from a street stall near the pier upon arrival (~80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village Night Market — try grilled skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh spring rolls from street vendors (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance if possible. Shared minivan + ferry combos from Phuket to Phi Phi cost around 350–500 THB. October is shoulder/wet season — occasional rain showers are possible, so pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to Tonsai Beach for a sunrise walk. Rent a kayak (200–300 THB/hour) and paddle along the coastline toward Loh Dalum Bay. Enjoy the calm morning waters before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget long-tail boat tour to the iconic Maya Bay (reopened with visitor limits), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave. These group tours typically cost 400–600 THB per person and depart from Tonsai Pier around midday.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don, shower, and head to the hilltop viewpoint for a panoramic sunset view over both bays — it's a short but steep 20-minute hike and completely free.

meals.breakfast: Local Thai breakfast at a small café near Tonsai — rice porridge (jok) or toast with eggs (~80–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the boat tour, or grab a quick meal at a beachside shack before departure (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Reggae Bar area street food stalls — pad see ew, som tam, and fresh coconut water (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has a daily visitor cap — confirm tour includes an official entry permit. Wear reef-safe sunscreen. Bring cash as many vendors on the island are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Shark Point and Hin Klang reef near Phi Phi Don — rent basic snorkel gear from a local shop (100–150 THB) and join a budget group longtail boat trip. Look out for blacktip reef sharks and colorful coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Monkey Beach (Hat Ling) by longtail boat — a short 10-minute ride from Tonsai (~200 THB return). Observe the macaques from a safe distance. Afterward, relax on Loh Dalum Bay beach.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Phi Phi's famous fire show on the beach near Tonsai Bay — free to watch, typically starts around 8–9 PM. Browse beachfront bars for cheap Chang beer buckets.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh fruit shake from a beachside vendor (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside shack near Loh Dalum — grilled fish with rice and papaya salad (~150–180 THB)
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant in Tonsai Village — green curry or massaman curry with rice (~120–160 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Do not feed the monkeys at Monkey Beach — they can be aggressive. Keep valuables secured on the boat. October weather may bring afternoon rain, so plan outdoor activities for the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Phi Phi to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5 hours, ~250–350 THB). Check into a budget guesthouse near Chao Fa Pier or the night market area. Drop your bags and head out to explore Krabi Town on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram (free entry) — a beautiful hilltop temple with sweeping views over Krabi Town. Then walk along the riverside promenade and browse the local market stalls near Chao Fa Park.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's famous Walking Street Night Market (open Thursday–Sunday) or the Chao Fa Night Market for incredible cheap street food and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Eat before boarding the ferry — grab a roti with banana and condensed milk from a street stall (~40–60 THB)
meals.lunch: Krabi Town local restaurant — khao man gai (chicken rice) or boat noodles (~60–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Chao Fa Night Market — pad thai, satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh-squeezed juices (~150–200 THB for a full spread)

day_by_day.notes: Krabi Town is a great base for exploring the surrounding region. Budget guesthouses here cost 300–600 THB/night. Confirm your next day's longtail boat or tour from the pier.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Krabi Town or Ao Nang to the Four Islands Tour — includes Koh Mor, Koh Chueak, Koh Tub, and Koh Kai (Chicken Island). Budget group tours cost around 500–700 THB including snorkeling gear and a simple lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at the stunning Emerald Cave area and relax on the sandbar connecting Koh Tub and Koh Mor at low tide — a surreal natural phenomenon. Return to Krabi by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ao Nang Beach (30-minute songthaew ride from Krabi Town, ~50 THB) for a beach walk at dusk. Browse the Ao Nang beachfront strip for cheap eats and cold drinks.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or nearby café — toast, eggs, and coffee (~80–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Included simple Thai lunch on the Four Islands Tour (typically rice, fish, and fruit)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang beachfront food stalls — grilled seafood platter, sticky rice, and fresh coconut (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The sandbar at Koh Tub is only accessible at low tide — check tide charts before booking. Wear water shoes as the seabed can be rocky. Bring a dry bag for your phone and valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Take a songthaew to Railay Beach (accessible only by longtail boat from Ao Nang, ~100 THB each way). Explore West Railay Beach and East Railay Beach, then hike up to the famous Phra Nang Cave and Princess Cave shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing on Railay's world-class limestone cliffs — beginner half-day courses with a local guide cost around 800–1,000 THB including equipment. Alternatively, kayak around the dramatic karst formations (~300 THB/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset from West Railay Beach — one of the most photogenic spots in all of Thailand. Take the longtail back to Ao Nang and enjoy dinner before returning to Krabi.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang street stall — fresh fruit, fried dough (pa thong ko), and Thai iced tea (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Railay Beach café — simple pad thai or fried rice (~150–180 THB); slightly pricier due to remote location
meals.dinner: Ao Nang night market or local restaurant — tom yum soup with rice (~120–160 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is car-free and only accessible by boat. Wear proper footwear for the cave hike — it can be muddy. The Princess Cave has religious significance; dress respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — take a songthaew from Krabi Town (~30 THB). Climb the famous 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking 360-degree views over Krabi's jungle and karst landscape. Start early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Krabi's hot springs at Khlong Thom (budget songthaew or shared taxi, ~200–300 THB return). Soak in natural warm mineral pools surrounded by jungle — entry is approximately 90 THB.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town and spend the evening exploring the riverside area. Visit a local Thai massage shop for a budget foot massage (200–250 THB for 1 hour) to recover from the temple climb.

meals.breakfast: Local market near Krabi Town — rice soup with pork and a Thai iced coffee (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the hot springs visit, or eat at a simple roadside stall near Khlong Thom (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town local restaurant — massaman curry, jasmine rice, and fresh watermelon juice (~150–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — bring plenty of water and start before 9 AM to avoid midday heat. Wear modest clothing as it is an active temple. The hot springs are naturally warm (35–40°C) and very relaxing.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry or speedboat from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 1.5–2 hours, ~350–500 THB). Check into a budget bungalow or guesthouse near Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao). Unpack and take a slow walk along the 4km stretch of Long Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (200–250 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta Old Town — a charming stilted fishing village with colorful wooden shophouses, local art galleries, and a relaxed vibe. Browse the small local market.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the western coast — Koh Lanta is famous for its fiery sunsets. Head to a beachfront bar for a cheap sunset drink and enjoy the laid-back island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat before boarding the ferry — grab a banana roti or noodle soup in Krabi (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Koh Lanta Old Town local restaurant — seafood fried rice or spicy stir-fry with river fish (~120–160 THB)
meals.dinner: Long Beach beachfront food stall or budget restaurant — grilled prawns, som tam, and sticky rice (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less touristy than Phi Phi — great for budget travelers. Scooter rental requires a valid license; ride carefully as roads can be narrow. October may bring some rain but the island remains beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island (entry ~200 THB). Explore the jungle trails, lighthouse, and pristine beaches. Snorkel in the clear waters around the park's coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Klong Nin Beach — one of Koh Lanta's most beautiful and quieter beaches. Swim, sunbathe, and relax. If the weather is good, join a budget snorkeling trip to nearby Koh Rok (600–800 THB, includes gear and lunch).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach area and explore the local night market near Ban Saladan (the main pier town) for cheap street food and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or beachside café — banana pancakes and fresh juice (~100–130 THB)
meals.lunch: Included on the Koh Rok snorkel trip, or beachside shack near Klong Nin (~150 THB)
meals.dinner: Ban Saladan night market — pad kra pao (basil stir-fry with egg), fresh coconut, and mango sorbet (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok has some of the best coral in the Andaman Sea — highly recommended if weather permits. The national park lighthouse offers stunning views. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Kayaking and mangrove exploration at Koh Lanta's eastern coast — rent a kayak (~300 THB/half day) and paddle through the mangrove forests near the old town. Look for monitor lizards, birds, and small fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Kantiang Bay — arguably Koh Lanta's most scenic beach, with dramatic hills, clear water, and a quiet atmosphere. Take a swim and enjoy the natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Thai cooking class in the evening (some guesthouses and local operators offer 3-hour classes for 800–1,000 THB including ingredients and a meal). Learn to make pad thai, green curry, and mango sticky rice.

meals.breakfast: Local market near Long Beach — sticky rice with grilled pork and papaya salad (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Small local restaurant near Kantiang Bay — fish curry with rice and a fresh lime soda (~130–160 THB)
meals.dinner: Eat your cooking class creations! Or grab additional street food near your guesthouse (~100 THB supplement)

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is excellent value — you eat what you cook and take home a recipe card. Book in advance as class sizes are small. The mangrove kayak is best done in the morning when wildlife is most active.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry from Koh Lanta back to Krabi, then connect to Phuket via shared minivan (total journey ~3–4 hours, ~400–600 THB combined). Check into a budget hostel or guesthouse in Patong or Kata Beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kata Beach or Karon Beach — quieter and more budget-friendly alternatives to Patong. Take a swim, rent a beach chair (50–100 THB), and enjoy the Andaman Sea views. Walk along the coastal road for ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Patong's famous Bangla Road night scene — lively street performances, night market stalls, and cheap street food. Window shop and soak up the buzzing atmosphere without spending much.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing Koh Lanta — guesthouse breakfast or roadside stall (~100 THB)
meals.lunch: Grab food during the journey at a roadside rest stop — khao man gai or noodle soup (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Patong street food stalls near Bangla Road — pad thai, satay, spring rolls, and fresh fruit shakes (~200 THB for a full meal)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket can be more expensive than the islands — stick to local restaurants and street food to stay on budget. Avoid tourist trap restaurants near the beach. A songthaew between Patong and Kata costs ~30–50 THB.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Big Buddha (Phra Phutta Ming Mongkol Akenakkiri) on Nakkerd Hill — free entry, stunning views over Phuket and the Andaman Sea. Dress modestly (sarongs available at the entrance). Nearby Wat Chalong temple is also free and worth visiting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-listed area with beautiful Sino-Portuguese shophouses, street art murals, and local cafés. Walk along Thalang Road and Soi Rommanee for the best photo opportunities. Browse the weekend market if visiting on Saturday or Sunday.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Promthep Cape for the most famous sunset viewpoint in Phuket (free). Afterward, visit the Phuket Night Market (Naka Weekend Market or Malin Plaza) for cheap local food and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Phuket Old Town café — kaya toast, soft-boiled eggs, and kopi (local coffee) (~100–130 THB)
meals.lunch: Phuket Old Town local restaurant — Phuket-style hokkien noodles or dim sum (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Malin Plaza or local night market — grilled seafood, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut water (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Big Buddha is most beautiful in the early morning light. Tuk-tuks in Phuket are expensive — use songthaews or Grab app for budget transport.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — wake up early for one last sunrise walk on Kata Beach or Karon Beach. Take a refreshing swim in the Andaman Sea. Pick up last-minute souvenirs from local market stalls (dried mango, coconut snacks, Thai spices) near your guesthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit a final local street food spot for a farewell Thai meal. Head to Phuket International Airport via shared minivan or Grab (~150–250 THB from Patong/Kata). Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Thailand with incredible memories of beaches, islands, and street food adventures. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — jok (rice porridge) with pork and ginger, or khao tom at a local market (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or a last street food meal near your guesthouse — pad kra pao or green curry (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Pack dried Thai snacks and instant noodles from 7-Eleven as affordable gifts. Double-check your ferry and transport bookings the night before. Keep some cash for airport transport and any last-minute expenses. Total estimated daily budget: 800–1,500 THB/day (approx. $22–$42 USD) excluding accommodation.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — skip morning activities. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Phi Phi Islands via ferry from Krabi or Phuket pier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the afternoon ferry to Phi Phi Don Island (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Enjoy scenic views of limestone karsts and turquoise Andaman Sea en route. Check in to your Boutique Stay on Phi Phi Islands and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Village's main walking street. Explore the local night market and get oriented with the island layout. Watch the sunset from the Phi Phi Viewpoint if energy allows (20-minute hike from the village).

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at Krabi or Phuket airport before boarding the ferry
meals.lunch: Quick bite at a pier-side café near the ferry terminal — try a Thai green curry or pad see ew (150–200 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at local Tonsai Village restaurant such as Papaya Restaurant — try massaman curry with jasmine rice and a fresh fruit shake (250–350 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during October as it is still shoulder/high season. Keep important documents and valuables in your carry-on during the boat transfer. October may bring occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise walk to Phi Phi Viewpoint (Koh Phi Phi Don). The 20-minute hike rewards you with a stunning panoramic view of both bays. Return for a relaxed breakfast near the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Leh, visiting Maya Bay (The Beach), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave. Swim in crystal-clear waters and observe vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and explore the beachfront bars along Loh Dalum Bay. Enjoy fire show performances that typically start around 9 PM at the beach bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — fresh fruit smoothie bowl and toast (120–180 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from a local vendor before the boat tour, or eat at a beachside shack near Maya Bay — grilled fish with sticky rice (200–280 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Tonsai Village walking street — try pad thai, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut (150–250 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor hours and quotas to protect the ecosystem — confirm timings with your tour operator. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. Snorkeling gear is usually provided on tours.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or join a guided kayaking tour around the eastern coastline of Phi Phi Don, paddling through hidden coves and shallow turquoise lagoons. Explore Monkey Beach (Ao Ling) by boat or kayak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Long Beach (Hat Yao) on the southern tip of Phi Phi Don via a short longtail boat ride. Relax on the quieter, less crowded beach, swim, and sunbathe. Enjoy the calmer waters ideal for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai for a Thai cooking class or a sunset cocktail cruise around the island (many operators offer 2-hour sunset cruises departing around 5 PM).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery in Tonsai — banana pancake and fresh orange juice (100–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Long Beach — grilled prawns, som tum (papaya salad), and Chang beer (280–380 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant in Tonsai Village — recommended for their Thai curries and seafood dishes (300–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats to Long Beach cost approximately 100–150 THB per person. Monkeys at Monkey Beach can be aggressive — do not feed them and keep bags zipped. Sunset cruises typically cost 600–900 THB per person.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5 hours). Check in to a mid-range guesthouse in Krabi Town or head directly to Ao Nang Beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the iconic Railay Beach via a 15-minute longtail boat from Ao Nang (accessible only by boat due to limestone cliffs). Visit Phra Nang Cave Beach and the famous Princess Cave shrine. Swim and explore the dramatic karst scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang by longtail and explore the Ao Nang Walking Street for street food, souvenirs, and local nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Tonsai Village before catching the ferry — coffee and roti with banana and condensed milk (80–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Railay Beach — fresh seafood platter with steamed rice (300–400 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food at Ao Nang Night Market — tom yum soup, grilled satay sticks, and mango sticky rice (200–300 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats to Railay Beach from Ao Nang cost approximately 100 THB per person each way. Railay can get crowded in the afternoon — aim to arrive before noon. Store your luggage at your accommodation while day-tripping.

day_by_day.morning: Join a 4-Island Tour departing from Krabi or Ao Nang — visiting Koh Mook, Koh Kradan, Koh Libong, and Koh Ngai. Snorkel at Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot) on Koh Mook, swimming through a dark sea tunnel to a hidden beach inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour with beach time at Koh Kradan, known for its crystal-clear waters and vibrant coral gardens. Snorkel among colorful reef fish and soft corals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi/Ao Nang by late afternoon. Relax and enjoy a Thai massage on the beach strip (60-minute traditional massage: 300–400 THB).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near Ao Nang — eggs, toast, fruit plate (150–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Included buffet lunch on the boat tour or picnic on a beach island — typically provided by tour operators
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant in Krabi Town — try the local specialty, Krabi-style stir-fried crab with curry powder (350–500 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: 4-Island Tours typically cost 800–1,200 THB per person including lunch, snorkeling gear, and longtail/speedboat transfers. Book the day before at any tour shop in Ao Nang. October weather may cause occasional swells — check sea conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) in Krabi Town — climb 1,237 steps to the hilltop for panoramic views of Krabi's landscape. Start early to avoid midday heat. The temple complex at the base is also worth exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Krabi Town's local market and the riverside promenade. Visit the quirky Krabi Town Walking Street area and browse local handicrafts, fresh produce, and street snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Take a boat trip along the mangrove-lined Krabi River for a sunset cruise, spotting wildlife including macaques, sea eagles, and monitor lizards in their natural habitat.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near Tiger Cave Temple — local Thai-style breakfast of rice porridge (jok) with century egg and ginger (80–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Krabi Town's local market — authentic Thai dishes like khao man gai (chicken rice) or boat noodles (60–100 THB per dish)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant in Krabi Town — fresh grilled fish, morning glory stir-fry, and steamed jasmine rice (250–350 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes and bring plenty of water. Modest dress is required at the temple (cover shoulders and knees). The sunset mangrove cruise typically costs 400–600 THB per person.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Krabi to Koh Lanta by ferry or minivan (approximately 2 hours). Check in to a mid-range bungalow resort on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) or Klong Nin Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore Koh Lanta's scenic coastal road. Visit the charming Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) on the eastern coast — a historic fishing village with Sino-Portuguese shophouses, wooden piers, and a relaxed atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset from the western beaches of Koh Lanta — Long Beach or Sunset Beach are ideal. Enjoy the famous Koh Lanta laid-back evening vibe.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi accommodation or a café before departure — fresh fruit smoothie and toast (100–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a seafood restaurant in Old Town Koh Lanta — steamed fish with lime and chili, coconut soup (250–350 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner at Long Beach — barbecued seafood platter, green papaya salad, and coconut ice cream (300–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Koh Lanta from Krabi runs seasonally — confirm schedules in advance. Scooter rental costs approximately 200–300 THB per day. Old Town is best explored on foot and is a great spot for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day snorkeling trip to the Koh Lanta Marine National Park — visiting Koh Rok Nok and Koh Rok Nai, two uninhabited islands with some of the best coral reefs in the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at Koh Ha (Five Islands), known for its spectacular underwater caverns, swim-throughs, and diverse marine life including leopard sharks and sea turtles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Unwind with a beachside yoga session (many resorts offer evening classes) or a traditional Thai herbal compress massage.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your resort before the tour departure — Thai omelette with rice and fresh juice (120–180 THB)
meals.lunch: Buffet lunch included on the snorkeling tour, typically served on the boat or a beach on Koh Rok
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango House Restaurant or a similar beachfront spot on Long Beach — massaman lamb curry and roti (350–500 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok and Koh Ha snorkeling tours cost approximately 1,200–1,800 THB per person including gear, lunch, and park fees. Sea conditions in October can vary — tours may be cancelled in rough weather. Always check with operators the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mu Ko Lanta National Park on the southern tip of Koh Lanta — hike through jungle trails to a lighthouse with sweeping views of the Andaman Sea. Look out for wildlife including hornbills and monitor lizards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Klong Nin Beach or Bamboo Bay — quieter beaches on the southern end of the island with fewer crowds. Swim, read, and soak in the natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Head back north to the main beach strip for a street food evening. Visit the Koh Lanta Night Market (held regularly in the high season) for local dishes, fresh seafood, and tropical fruit.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near your resort — banana pancakes, fresh fruit plate, and iced coffee (100–160 THB)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near the national park or at a small roadside stall — grilled chicken skewers, sticky rice, and papaya salad (150–200 THB)
meals.dinner: Night market dinner — try a mix of dishes: pad kra pao (basil stir-fry), grilled squid, and fresh coconut water (200–300 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: National park entrance fee is approximately 200 THB for foreigners. Bring insect repellent for the jungle hike. The lighthouse trail takes about 30–45 minutes one way and offers excellent photo opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Koh Lanta to Phuket by ferry and minivan combination (approximately 3–4 hours). Check in to a mid-range hotel in Patong, Kata, or Karon Beach area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kata Beach or Karon Beach for a relaxed afternoon swim. These beaches are less hectic than Patong and offer beautiful scenery with golden sand and clear water. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Phuket's famous Bangla Road in Patong for the vibrant nightlife atmosphere. Alternatively, visit the lively Karon Night Market for a more local experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Koh Lanta resort before departure — eggs, toast, fresh juice (150–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a roadside restaurant during the transfer stop — pad thai or fried rice (100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Kata — grilled tiger prawns, tom kha gai (coconut chicken soup), and steamed rice (300–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry and minivan transfers in advance. The journey involves multiple vehicle changes — keep your luggage manageable. Kata and Karon are recommended over Patong for a more relaxed mid-range experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Phang Nga Bay — join a tour by longtail boat or sea kayak to explore the dramatic limestone karsts, sea caves, and mangrove channels. Visit the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan) and Ko Panyi floating village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Phang Nga Bay with a sea kayaking session through hidden hongs (inland lagoons accessible only at low tide). Paddle through cathedral-like cave openings into serene enclosed lagoons.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket by late afternoon. Head to Phuket Old Town for an evening stroll along the colorful Sino-Portuguese streets, visiting street art, local cafés, and the Sunday Walking Street market.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before departure — continental breakfast or Thai-style congee (150–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Ko Panyi floating village — fresh steamed fish, stir-fried vegetables, and rice (250–350 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Phuket Old Town — try the local specialty, Hokkien mee noodles or Phuket-style lobster yellow curry at a heritage café (300–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay tours cost approximately 1,200–2,000 THB per person depending on whether you choose speedboat or longtail, and whether sea kayaking is included. Book the day before at any tour desk. The Sunday Walking Street in Old Town is a highlight — don't miss it if visiting on a Sunday.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Big Buddha (Phra Phutta Ming Mongkol Akenakkiri) on Nakkerd Hill — a 45-meter white marble statue offering panoramic views over Phuket. Explore the temple grounds and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Promthep Cape on the southern tip of Phuket for stunning coastal scenery. Then visit Rawai Beach to browse the local seafood market — choose your own fresh seafood and have it cooked at a nearby restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final Phuket evening with a Thai cultural show or Muay Thai boxing match at a local stadium (tickets: 1,000–1,500 THB ringside). Alternatively, enjoy a farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café in your hotel area — acai bowl, fresh fruit, and Thai iced tea (150–200 THB)
meals.lunch: Rawai seafood market experience — select fresh prawns, crab, and fish, then have them grilled or steamed at a market-side restaurant (400–600 THB for a generous spread)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Phuket Old Town or Kata — Thai tasting menu with panoramic views (500–700 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Big Buddha is free to enter but donations are welcome. Dress modestly (sarongs available to borrow). Rawai seafood market is a unique experience — prices are per kilogram and negotiating is acceptable. Check Muay Thai schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final morning swim at your chosen Phuket beach. Visit a local market for last-minute souvenir shopping — Thai silk scarves, elephant pants, local spices, and artisan crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your hotel and transfer to Phuket International Airport. Allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Enjoy a final Thai meal at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phuket. Reflect on 13 incredible days of island hopping, street food adventures, and Andaman Sea exploration.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — khao tom (rice soup) with ginger and century egg, or fresh fruit smoothie bowl at a beachside café (100–150 THB)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Phuket airport or a nearby restaurant before check-in — pad see ew or green curry with jasmine rice (150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Airport is approximately 30–45 minutes from Patong/Kata depending on traffic. Pre-book your airport transfer for peace of mind (300–500 THB by taxi or 150–200 THB by shared minivan). Declare any food items when passing through customs. Keep receipts for VAT refund claims on eligible purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer from Krabi or Phuket pier to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to your boutique luxury resort, unwind on the private terrace, and enjoy a welcome drink while soaking in panoramic Andaman Sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along Ton Sai Bay promenade. Explore the vibrant beachfront atmosphere as the sky turns golden over the limestone karsts.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: Not applicable — en route to Phi Phi
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi — a beloved fine-casual spot serving Thai classics and fresh seafood. Try the massaman curry and grilled barramundi with jasmine rice.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private speedboat transfer in advance for a seamless arrival experience. Confirm check-in time with the boutique resort. October may bring occasional afternoon showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat tour to Maya Bay — arrive early before day-trippers to experience the iconic lagoon in near-solitude. Snorkel the crystal-clear waters around Loh Samah Bay and Pileh Lagoon, teeming with colorful reef fish and coral formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely poolside lunch. Afterward, join a guided kayaking excursion through the sea caves and hidden lagoons on the eastern side of Phi Phi Leh.
day_by_day.evening: Fire show and beachfront entertainment at Ton Sai Village. Enjoy cocktails at a beachside bar as local performers put on a spectacular fire dance display.

meals.breakfast: In-resort breakfast — fresh tropical fruit platter, eggs Benedict, and freshly brewed Thai coffee served on your private terrace.
meals.lunch: Poolside dining at the resort — grilled tiger prawns with garlic butter, green papaya salad, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: The Phi Phi Banyan Villa Restaurant — elegant open-air dining with panoramic bay views. Order the whole grilled sea bass in lemongrass and kaffir lime, paired with a chilled Sauvignon Blanc.

day_by_day.notes: Book your private longtail boat the evening before to secure an early morning departure. Maya Bay has restricted visitor hours — early arrival is essential. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and underwater camera.

day_by_day.morning: Guided rock climbing session on Phi Phi's iconic limestone cliffs with a certified instructor. The 'Tonsai Tower' route offers breathtaking aerial views of the bay. Suitable for beginners and experienced climbers alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Phi Phi Viewpoint via a scenic 20-minute hike through the jungle. The panoramic twin-bay vista is one of the most photographed views in Thailand. Descend and explore the local village market for handcrafted souvenirs and fresh tropical snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Private beach dinner experience arranged by the resort — a candlelit table set directly on the sand with personalized menu, dedicated butler service, and the sound of gentle waves as your backdrop.

meals.breakfast: In-resort — Thai-style congee with century egg and ginger, tropical smoothie bowl, and freshly squeezed watermelon juice.
meals.lunch: Local street food exploration at Ton Sai Village — pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) with fried egg from a beloved local stall, fresh mango sticky rice for dessert.
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner curated by the resort chef — five-course tasting menu featuring tom kha gai soup, lobster thermidor, and a coconut panna cotta with passion fruit coulis.

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner must be reserved at least 48 hours in advance through the concierge. Wear sturdy shoes for the viewpoint hike. Rock climbing gear is provided by the guide service.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium island-hopping excursion departing by private speedboat. First stop: Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) — a pristine, largely uninhabited island with powdery white sand and turquoise shallows. Snorkel the surrounding reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for world-class snorkeling among vibrant coral gardens and sea turtles. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch served on the boat with fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and chilled beverages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi by late afternoon. Freshen up at the resort, then head out for an authentic Thai massage at a reputable spa — 90-minute traditional Thai massage with aromatic oils.

meals.breakfast: In-resort — American breakfast with smoked salmon, avocado toast, poached eggs, and a selection of fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the private speedboat — sushi rolls, chilled tiger prawns, fresh fruit skewers, artisan cheeses, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Pee Pee Bakery & Restaurant — a local institution known for its fresh seafood platters and wood-fired dishes. Try the garlic butter crab and tom yum soup.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the private speedboat itinerary the night before. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed. October waters can be slightly choppy — the speedboat captain will advise on conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the resort's beachfront deck led by a certified instructor. Follow with a refreshing ocean swim and a mindful morning walk along the quieter northern beach of Phi Phi Don.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scuba diving experience with a PADI-certified dive center. Explore the legendary 'King Cruiser Wreck' or 'Shark Point' — both accessible from Phi Phi and renowned for leopard sharks, moray eels, and vibrant reef life. Two guided dives included.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class with a local Thai chef — learn to prepare three classic dishes including pad thai, green curry, and mango sticky rice in a hands-on, intimate setting. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga in-resort breakfast — acai bowl, fresh coconut, granola with local honey, and herbal teas.
meals.lunch: At the dive center's beachside café — light bites including spring rolls, chicken satay skewers, and fresh lime soda.
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class, enjoyed with fellow participants and the host chef. Paired with Thai iced tea and local Singha beer.

day_by_day.notes: Diving certification is not required for the introductory dive, but notify the dive center of any medical conditions. The cooking class accommodates dietary restrictions — inform the host in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort — enjoy a late breakfast and unwind by the infinity pool overlooking the Andaman Sea. Optional: visit the resort's spa for a 60-minute Thai herbal compress massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer to Krabi Town (approximately 45 minutes). Explore the vibrant Krabi Town Walking Street market and the iconic Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for a spectacular 360° view over the province.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's famous night market — Chao Fa Night Market. Sample an array of street food including satay, pad see ew, fresh oysters, and Thai crepes (roti).

meals.breakfast: In-resort — full Thai breakfast with khao tom (rice soup), steamed buns, tropical fruit, and Thai iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Krabi Town — khao pad (fried rice) with crab, tom yum goong (spicy shrimp soup), and fresh coconut ice cream.
meals.dinner: Street food feast at Chao Fa Night Market — grilled skewers, pad thai from a wok stall, fresh spring rolls, and mango sticky rice for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Tiger Cave Temple climb — it is strenuous but highly rewarding. Dress modestly when visiting the temple (shoulders and knees covered). Return speedboat to Phi Phi departs by 21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat tour to the stunning Railay Beach — accessible only by boat, this dramatic peninsula is flanked by towering limestone cliffs. Explore Phra Nang Cave Beach and the sacred Princess Cave shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through the mangrove forests of Ao Thalane near Krabi — a guided eco-tour through serene waterways teeming with wildlife including monitor lizards, kingfishers, and macaques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi for a relaxed evening. Rooftop cocktails at the resort bar as the sun sets behind the karst silhouettes, followed by a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-resort — eggs your way, fresh-pressed orange juice, croissants, and a tropical fruit platter.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Railay Beach — fresh seafood barbecue with grilled lobster, prawns, and squid served with sticky rice and som tam (papaya salad).
meals.dinner: In-resort fine dining — red duck curry with lychee and jasmine rice, followed by sticky toffee pudding with Thai tea ice cream.

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is best visited mid-morning to avoid peak crowds. The mangrove kayaking tour lasts approximately 3 hours — book through the concierge. Bring insect repellent for the mangrove tour.

day_by_day.morning: Stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) lesson and guided tour around the calm waters of Phi Phi Don's eastern coastline. A peaceful and scenic way to explore hidden coves and sea caves at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Phi Phi's local fishing village on the northern tip of the island — interact with local fishermen, observe traditional boat-building, and browse artisan craft stalls. Photography enthusiasts will find extraordinary subjects here.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise aboard a private chartered longtail boat — circumnavigate Phi Phi Leh as the sky ignites in shades of orange and pink. Champagne and canapés served on board.

meals.breakfast: In-resort — banana pancakes with coconut cream, fresh fruit, and Thai-style iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Local eatery in the fishing village — freshly caught grilled fish with steamed rice, stir-fried morning glory, and fresh coconut water served in the shell.
meals.dinner: Romantic in-resort dinner on your private terrace — chef's selection of three-course Thai-French fusion menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: The sunset cruise must be booked through the concierge at least one day in advance. SUP equipment is available through the resort's water sports center. Bring a waterproof phone case.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Koh Lanta — a longer island known for its laid-back atmosphere, diverse beaches, and rich Malay-Thai cultural heritage. Depart by private speedboat (approximately 1.5 hours from Phi Phi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta Old Town — a charming stilted fishing village with colorful shophouses, local galleries, and artisan boutiques. Visit the Lanta Animal Welfare center and the Sea Gypsy village.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — one of Koh Lanta's finest stretches of sand. Dine at a beachfront restaurant before the return speedboat to Phi Phi.

meals.breakfast: In-resort — full continental spread with cold cuts, cheeses, pastries, and freshly brewed coffee.
meals.lunch: Time for a Bite Restaurant, Koh Lanta Old Town — a beloved local spot with authentic southern Thai cuisine. Try the massaman curry and fresh fish cakes.
meals.dinner: Somewhere Else Restaurant, Koh Lanta — beachfront fine dining with panoramic sea views. Signature whole steamed fish with ginger and black bean sauce, paired with a crisp Riesling.

day_by_day.notes: Depart Phi Phi by 08:30 to maximize time on Koh Lanta. Return speedboat departs Koh Lanta by 19:30. Koh Lanta's Old Town is best explored on foot or by rented bicycle.

day_by_day.morning: Wellness morning — 90-minute couple's spa treatment at the resort's luxury spa. Choose from traditional Thai massage, aromatherapy, or a rejuvenating body scrub using locally sourced coconut and turmeric.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided snorkeling tour to the lesser-known Bida Nok and Bida Nai islands — two small islets south of Phi Phi Leh with exceptional visibility and abundant marine life including whale sharks (seasonal), reef sharks, and manta rays.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive beachfront barbecue dinner organized by the resort — a curated selection of premium meats, whole lobsters, tiger prawns, and fresh catch grilled to order under the stars.

meals.breakfast: In-resort — overnight oats with mango and coconut milk, smoked salmon bagel, and a green detox smoothie.
meals.lunch: Light snacks and fresh fruit on the snorkeling boat — energy bars, tropical fruit, and chilled sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Resort beachfront BBQ — whole lobster, wagyu beef skewers, grilled corn, and a decadent Thai coconut tart for dessert. Paired with a selection of premium wines and cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Whale shark sightings at Bida Nok/Nai are more common between October and April — October is an excellent time. Always maintain a respectful distance from marine life. Spa treatments should be reserved two days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Chartered private speedboat day trip to Koh Rok — a remote, pristine island cluster approximately 2 hours from Phi Phi, renowned for its crystal-clear turquoise waters, white sand beaches, and some of the best snorkeling in the Andaman Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring Koh Rok Nai and Koh Rok Nok — snorkel the shallow coral gardens, laze on untouched beaches, and enjoy the extraordinary solitude of this protected marine park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi by early evening. Relax at the resort and enjoy a quiet, indulgent evening with in-room dining and a private movie setup on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: In-resort — Thai-style breakfast with jok (rice porridge), fried dough (patongo), and fresh fruit.
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on Koh Rok beach — charcuterie board, smoked salmon, artisan bread, tropical fruit, and chilled rosé wine.
meals.dinner: In-room private dining — chef-prepared five-course Thai tasting menu including yam woon sen (glass noodle salad), gaeng keow wan (green curry), and sticky rice with durian ice cream.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is a national marine park — entrance fees apply. No overnight stays permitted. Depart Phi Phi by 07:00 for a full day on the island. Bring sufficient sunscreen and drinking water.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Phi Phi — take a reflective sunrise walk along the beach, collect your thoughts, and photograph the magical golden light over the Andaman Sea. Optional: final snorkel or swim from the resort's private beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and check out of the boutique resort. Private speedboat transfer back to Krabi or Phuket. Depending on your onward journey, explore Phuket's Old Town — a UNESCO-recognized heritage area with Sino-Portuguese architecture, vibrant street art, and excellent street food.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner in Phuket — celebrate your Thailand journey with a spectacular meal at one of Phuket's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final in-resort breakfast — a lavish spread of your favorites from the trip, including fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and Thai iced tea.
meals.lunch: Street food exploration in Phuket Old Town — o-tao (oyster omelette), moo hong (braised pork belly), and fresh roti with condensed milk.
meals.dinner: Acqua Restaurant, Phuket — award-winning Italian-Mediterranean fine dining with Andaman seafood. Try the Phuket lobster linguine and tiramisu. Paired with an excellent Italian wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time at the Phi Phi resort is typically 12:00 — arrange luggage storage if needed. Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot. Book the farewell dinner reservation well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Phuket — visit Wat Chalong, Phuket's most important Buddhist temple, for a serene cultural experience. Browse the Sunday Walking Street market (if applicable) or explore the Phuket weekend market for last-minute gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon at leisure — optional visit to Promthep Cape for sweeping panoramic views over the southern tip of Phuket. Transfer to Phuket International Airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phuket — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phuket — full buffet spread with international and Thai options.
meals.lunch: Final street food lunch near Phuket Old Town — khao man gai (poached chicken rice), fresh spring rolls, and Thai milk tea from a local vendor.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal on departure.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Phuket International Airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Ensure all souvenirs comply with customs regulations — particularly fresh fruits and certain wood products. Keep a small amount of Thai Baht for last-minute purchases.
